chapter: New York dance bands and Dorsey
title: Joining Tommy Dorsey: freedom to solo
summary: Freeman joined Dorsey in 1936 alongside Dave Tough and Max Kaminsky and was happy because Dorsey let him play many choruses.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: You were with Tommy a good while, weren't you?
I was with Tommy at least two years. It's difficult to remember because I think I joined him
in 1936 and I remember Dave Tough was in the band, Max Kaminsky, Tommy --
How long was Dave in the band?
Dave was in the band before I got into it. And I was with Tommy about, certainly two years, and I think Dave was with him a little longer.
Were you happy in that band?
Bud, you were just telling me that you enjoyed it in that band, but you hadn't yet told me why. Will you go ahead from there?

Although it was essentially a dance band, and Tommy had to feature his beautiful solo playing, he loved jazz soloists and whenever he could get one, if the price was right, he would bring them in the band.

I think if Tommy had had his way, he would have had a complete 18-piece jazz band, but he was selling dance music and of course, his beautiful melodic trombone and dance music was the thing in those days. But, again, to answer your question I was happy most of the time because Tommy let me play almost every tune we played that he wasn't featured on, he let me play several choruses.
When we played in theatres, I'd get out in front of the band for maybe 10 or 15 minutes and play. It was incredible, maybe 20 or 30 choruses on a song and
